caution: See a doctor or dentist if an ulcer lasts more than three weeks, is very large, or you have fever or cannot drink.
warning_signs_to_escalate: lasting more than three weeks; cannot drink; fever

typical_symptoms: red eye; itchy eyes; watery eyes; eye discharge; gritty feeling in eye
description: Redness, itching, and watery or sticky discharge from one or both eyes, often with a gritty sensation.
recommendation: Home care with warm compresses and good hygiene is usually appropriate. See a doctor if symptoms worsen, vision changes, or it doesn't improve after a few days.
caution: Do not share towels or pillows, and see a doctor urgently for eye pain, light sensitivity or reduced vision.
warning_signs_to_escalate: eye pain; vision change; light sensitivity; newborn with eye discharge
self_care: Wash hands, avoid touching or sharing towels.

typical_symptoms: bleeding gums; red swollen gums; bad taste in mouth
description: Red, swollen gums that bleed when brushing, with bad breath.
recommendation: Brush gently twice a day, clean between teeth and see a dentist for cleaning.
caution: Seek care promptly for loose teeth, pus from the gums, facial swelling or fever.
warning_signs_to_escalate: pus; facial swelling; fever; loose teeth

typical_symptoms: bright red blood with stool; straining to pass stool; constipation; itching around anus; lump near anus
description: Bright red blood on the toilet paper or after passing stool, with itching, discomfort or a lump near the anus, often with constipation.
recommendation: Eat more fibre, drink water, avoid straining and sit in clean warm water for comfort. See a health worker to confirm the cause.
caution: Seek care promptly for heavy bleeding, black stools, dizziness, weight loss, or bowel changes lasting more than three weeks.
warning_signs_to_escalate: heavy bleeding; black stools; dizziness; weight loss

typical_symptoms: bright red blood with stool; hard stools; straining to pass stool; constipation
description: Sharp pain during and after passing a hard stool with a small amount of bright red blood.
recommendation: Eat fibre, drink plenty of water and soak in clean warm water. See a health worker if it lasts more than two weeks.
caution: Seek care for heavy bleeding, black stools, fever or a painful swelling near the anus.
warning_signs_to_escalate: heavy bleeding; black stools; fever; painful swelling

typical_symptoms: wound; bleeding from bite; broken skin; pain at sting site
description: A small cut, graze or puncture wound with light bleeding, without signs of infection.
recommendation: Press with a clean cloth until bleeding stops, wash well with clean running water and soap, cover with a clean dressing and check tetanus vaccination status.
caution: See a health worker the same day for a deep, dirty or rusty-object wound, or if tetanus vaccination is not up to date. Do not put soil, ash or herbs on wounds.
warning_signs_to_escalate: deep wound; bleeding that will not stop; spreading redness; pus; rusty object

typical_symptoms: red painful skin; blisters; peeling skin; heat exposure
description: Red, painful skin after too much sun, sometimes with blisters.
recommendation: Move out of the sun, cool the skin with clean cool water and drink extra fluids. Do not burst blisters.
caution: Seek care for large blisters, fever, confusion or faintness, which may mean heat illness.
warning_signs_to_escalate: large blisters; fever; confusion; fainting

typical_symptoms: rash in skin folds; itchy skin; heat exposure; red rash
description: Tiny itchy red bumps in sweaty areas such as the neck, back and skin folds in hot weather.
recommendation: Keep cool, wear loose cotton clothes, bathe with cool water and keep skin folds dry.
caution: See a health worker if there is pus, fever or the rash does not settle in a few days.
warning_signs_to_escalate: pus; fever; spreading rash

typical_symptoms: abdominal discomfort; itching around anus; visible worms in stool; loss of appetite; weight loss
description: Abdominal discomfort, poor appetite, itching around the anus, visible worms in stool and weight loss, mostly in children.
recommendation: See a health worker; deworming tablets are often provided through public programmes. Wash hands and trim nails.
caution: Seek care if severe abdominal pain, vomiting or yellow skin appear.
warning_signs_to_escalate: severe abdominal pain; vomiting; yellow skin

typical_symptoms: fever; muscle pain; cough; sore throat; runny nose; fatigue; chills; headache
description: Sudden fever with body aches, headache, cough, sore throat, runny nose and tiredness.
recommendation: Rest, drink fluids and take paracetamol for fever if needed. Stay home to avoid spreading it.
caution: See a doctor if breathing becomes difficult, symptoms last more than a week, or you are pregnant, elderly or have chronic illness.
warning_signs_to_escalate: difficulty breathing; chest pain; confusion

typical_symptoms: cough; phlegm; mild fever; tight chest; fatigue; wheezing
description: Cough with phlegm for several days after a cold, with mild chest discomfort and low fever.
recommendation: Rest, fluids and warm drinks. Avoid smoke and dust.
caution: See a doctor if cough lasts more than 3 weeks, there is breathlessness or blood in phlegm.
warning_signs_to_escalate: breathlessness; blood in phlegm; high fever

typical_symptoms: facial pain; congestion; thick nasal discharge; headache; reduced smell
description: Facial pain or pressure, blocked nose, thick nasal discharge and headache after a cold.
recommendation: Steam inhalation, fluids and rest. Saline nasal rinses may help.
caution: See a doctor if symptoms last over 10 days, or for severe headache, swelling around the eyes or high fever.
warning_signs_to_escalate: swelling around eyes; high fever; vision changes

typical_symptoms: sneezing; itchy eyes; itchy nose; runny nose; dust or pollen trigger
description: Repeated sneezing, itchy nose and eyes and clear runny nose, triggered by dust, pollen or seasons.
recommendation: Avoid triggers, wash bedding, and ask a pharmacist about antihistamines.
caution: See a doctor if wheeze, chest tightness or breathlessness occur.
warning_signs_to_escalate: wheezing; breathlessness

typical_symptoms: itchy blister rash; fever; fatigue; headache; blisters in different stages
description: Itchy blistering rash in different stages with mild fever and tiredness.
recommendation: Rest, fluids, keep nails short and calamine lotion for itch. Stay away from others until blisters crust.
caution: See a doctor promptly if pregnant, newborn, immune-weak, or if the rash becomes red and painful or you have breathing trouble.
warning_signs_to_escalate: pregnancy; newborn; breathing trouble; very high fever

typical_symptoms: intense itching worse at night; rash between fingers; family members itching; tiny skin burrows
description: Intense itching that is worse at night with tiny bumps or burrows between fingers and on the wrists; others in the home often itch too.
recommendation: See a health worker for scabies cream; treat all household members and wash clothes and bedding in hot water.
caution: Do not share clothes or bedding. Seek care if sores become red, hot or pus-filled.
warning_signs_to_escalate: pus-filled sores; spreading redness

typical_symptoms: ring-shaped rash; scaly skin; itchy skin; spreading patch
description: Ring-shaped, red, scaly and itchy skin patch with clearer centre that slowly spreads.
recommendation: Keep skin clean and dry; antifungal cream from a pharmacy or health worker. Avoid sharing towels.
caution: See a doctor if it spreads widely, involves the scalp or does not clear in 2 weeks.
warning_signs_to_escalate: scalp involvement; widespread rash

typical_symptoms: hives; itchy skin; raised welts
description: Itchy raised welts on the skin that come and go, without breathing or throat problems.
recommendation: Avoid the suspected trigger, cool compresses, and ask a pharmacist about antihistamines.
caution: Seek emergency care immediately if lips, tongue or throat swell or breathing becomes difficult.
warning_signs_to_escalate: swollen lips or tongue; difficulty breathing; dizziness

typical_symptoms: minor burn; red painful skin; small blisters
description: Small red painful burn or a few small blisters from hot water or flame, smaller than the palm.
recommendation: Cool under clean running water for 20 minutes, then cover with a clean non-stick dressing.
caution: Do not use ice, butter, oil, creams or toothpaste. Get medical care if the burn is larger than the person's hand, on the face, hands, feet or genitals, has white or charred skin, or is a chemical or electrical burn - and for any burn in a child under 5 or a pregnant woman.
warning_signs_to_escalate: larger than palm; burn on face or hands; child with burn; chemical or electrical burn; white or charred skin; child under five or pregnant woman

typical_symptoms: burning upper abdominal pain; bloating; nausea; belching; pain related to meals; heartburn
description: Burning pain in the upper abdomen, bloating, nausea and belching, often related to meals or spicy food.
recommendation: Eat small regular meals and avoid spicy food, alcohol, tobacco and painkillers such as ibuprofen. See a health worker if it persists beyond a week or two.
caution: Seek emergency care for vomiting blood, black stools or severe sudden abdominal pain.
warning_signs_to_escalate: vomiting blood; black stools; severe sudden pain

typical_symptoms: heartburn; sour taste in mouth; regurgitation; burning chest after meals; worse lying down
description: Burning in the chest after meals or lying down with sour taste or regurgitation.
recommendation: Eat smaller, earlier meals, avoid trigger foods, raise the head of the bed.
caution: Chest burning can sometimes be heart-related - seek emergency care if with sweating, breathlessness or spreading arm pain.
warning_signs_to_escalate: chest pain with sweating; difficulty swallowing; weight loss

typical_symptoms: high blood pressure reading; headache; dizzy; fatigue
description: High readings found on checking, sometimes with headache or dizziness, but often no symptoms.
recommendation: See a health worker within days to confirm readings and begin treatment. Reduce salt, stay active and avoid tobacco.
caution: Seek emergency care for very high readings with chest pain, severe headache, weakness or vision change.
warning_signs_to_escalate: chest pain; severe headache; weakness or speech trouble; vision change

typical_symptoms: increased thirst; frequent urination; fatigue; blurred vision; slow healing wounds; weight loss; tingling in feet
description: Increased thirst and urination, tiredness, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds and weight loss.
recommendation: See a health worker within days for a blood sugar test. Limit sugary drinks and stay active.
caution: Seek emergency care for vomiting, abdominal pain, fast breathing or drowsiness.
warning_signs_to_escalate: vomiting; fast breathing; drowsiness

typical_symptoms: fatigue; pale skin; dizzy; shortness of breath on exertion; palpitations; brittle nails
description: Tiredness, pale skin, dizziness, breathlessness on effort and palpitations, often from poor diet, worms or heavy periods.
recommendation: See a health worker for a haemoglobin test; iron-rich foods and iron-folic acid tablets are often available free in public programmes.
caution: Anaemia in pregnancy needs prompt review. Seek emergency care for chest pain, fainting or severe breathlessness.
warning_signs_to_escalate: fainting; chest pain; pregnancy; severe breathlessness

typical_symptoms: back pain; stiffness; muscle spasms; pain after lifting; pain worse with movement
description: Aching back after lifting or strain, stiff and worse with movement, without leg weakness.
recommendation: Stay gently active, apply heat, and avoid heavy lifting. Paracetamol may help.
caution: Seek emergency care for leg weakness, numbness around the groin, or loss of bladder or bowel control.
warning_signs_to_escalate: leg weakness; groin numbness; loss of bladder control

typical_symptoms: dull headache; band-like head pressure; neck tightness; stress
description: Dull band-like pressure around the head with neck tightness, linked to stress or poor sleep, without vomiting or aura.
recommendation: Rest, drink water, gentle neck stretches and paracetamol if needed.
caution: Seek care for sudden severe headache, fever with stiff neck, weakness or vision changes.
warning_signs_to_escalate: sudden severe headache; stiff neck with fever; weakness; vision change

typical_symptoms: insect sting; pain at sting site; swelling at sting site; redness; itchy skin
description: Pain, redness, swelling and itching at the site of a bee, wasp, ant or other insect sting or bite, without symptoms elsewhere in the body.
recommendation: Remove a visible sting by scraping it off sideways. Wash with clean water and soap, apply a cold cloth for pain and swelling, and keep the area clean. Avoid scratching.
caution: Hives all over the body, swelling of the face or lips, wheezing, dizziness or trouble breathing after a sting is an emergency. See a doctor if the swelling spreads widely, lasts more than a few days or becomes hot, pus-filled or very painful.
warning_signs_to_escalate: hives all over; swelling of face or lips; wheezing; dizziness; spreading redness

typical_symptoms: itchy rash after contact; red rash; blisters; dry cracked skin; itchy skin
description: Itchy red rash, sometimes with small blisters or dry cracked skin, appearing on skin that touched a plant, soap, detergent, jewellery, cosmetic or chemical.
recommendation: Wash the area with plain water and gentle soap and avoid the suspected trigger. Keep the skin moisturised. See a health worker if it does not improve in a week or keeps coming back.
caution: See a doctor promptly if the rash covers a large area, affects the face or genitals, becomes painful or oozing, or you have fever.
warning_signs_to_escalate: rash on face or genitals; oozing or pus; fever; rapid spread

typical_symptoms: dry itchy patches; rash in skin folds; itchy skin; dry cracked skin; family history of allergy
description: Long-lasting dry, very itchy patches of skin, often in skin folds such as elbows, behind the knees or on the face, that flare and settle, and often run in families with allergy or asthma.
recommendation: Moisturise regularly, use mild soap, keep nails short and avoid known triggers such as harsh soaps and wool. A health worker can advise on treatment for flares.
caution: See a doctor if the skin becomes red, painful, weeping or crusted (possible infection), or if sleep is badly affected. Do not apply strong steroid creams without medical advice.
warning_signs_to_escalate: weeping or crusted skin; fever; widespread painful rash

typical_symptoms: itchy eyes; watery eyes; red eye; sneezing; swollen eyelids; dust or pollen trigger
description: Both eyes itchy, red, watery and slightly swollen, often with sneezing, triggered by dust or pollen, without thick sticky discharge.
recommendation: Avoid rubbing the eyes, rinse with clean cool water, use a cold cloth and reduce exposure to dust or pollen. A pharmacist or health worker can advise on allergy eye drops.
caution: See a doctor urgently for eye pain, reduced vision, light sensitivity, or a red eye after an injury or in a contact-lens wearer.
warning_signs_to_escalate: eye pain; vision changes; light sensitivity

typical_symptoms: runny nose; sore throat; mild cough; sneezing; congestion; mild fever
description: Mild upper respiratory symptoms including runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, and low-grade fever, typically resolving within a week.
recommendation: Home care is appropriate. Rest, fluids, and over-the-counter symptom relief. See a doctor if symptoms worsen after 7-10 days.
caution: Antibiotics do not treat colds. Seek care if breathing becomes difficult, fever is high, or symptoms last more than 10 days.
warning_signs_to_escalate: difficulty breathing; high fever; symptoms over 10 days

typical_symptoms: honey coloured crusts; sores around mouth and nose; itchy skin; child under five
description: Red sores that break and form honey-coloured crusts, often around the nose and mouth, common in children and spreading easily.
recommendation: Gently wash the sores with soap and clean water, keep them covered, wash hands often and do not share towels. See a health worker, because antibiotic treatment is usually needed.
caution: See a doctor promptly if the sores spread quickly, there is fever, or the skin becomes very red and painful.
warning_signs_to_escalate: fever; spreading redness; very painful skin

typical_symptoms: itchy scalp; visible lice or nits; scratch marks on scalp
description: Itchy scalp with visible tiny lice or white egg cases (nits) stuck to the hair near the scalp, common in children.
recommendation: Treat with a lice product recommended by a pharmacist or health worker and comb the hair with a fine-toothed comb. Wash bedding and combs in hot water and check close contacts.
caution: Do not use kerosene or other harsh household chemicals on the scalp. See a health worker if sores on the scalp become infected.
warning_signs_to_escalate: infected sores on scalp; fever

typical_symptoms: nosebleed; dry nose; nose injury
description: Bleeding from one or both nostrils, often from dry air, nose picking, a minor knock or a cold.
recommendation: Sit up and lean forward, pinch the soft part of the nose firmly for 10 minutes without releasing, and breathe through the mouth. Do not tilt the head back.
caution: Seek urgent care if bleeding continues beyond 20 minutes despite pressure, follows a head injury, or the person feels faint, takes blood-thinning medicine, or has frequent nosebleeds.
warning_signs_to_escalate: bleeding longer than 20 minutes; after head injury; faintness

typical_symptoms: knee pain; joint pain; stiffness; pain on climbing stairs; pain worse with movement
description: Knee, hip or hand joint pain and stiffness that gets worse with activity and climbing stairs and eases with rest, mostly in older adults, without fever or redness.
recommendation: Keep gently active, maintain a healthy weight and use heat for stiffness. A health worker can advise on pain relief and exercises.
caution: See a doctor promptly if a joint is suddenly hot, red and swollen, you have fever, or you cannot bear weight.
warning_signs_to_escalate: hot red swollen joint; fever; unable to bear weight

typical_symptoms: constipation; hard stools; straining to pass stool; bloating; abdominal discomfort
description: Infrequent hard stools, straining and a bloated or uncomfortable abdomen, often related to low fibre or water intake.
recommendation: Increase fibre, fruit, vegetables and water and stay active. See a health worker if it persists for more than two weeks.
caution: Seek urgent care for severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, a swollen belly, blood in the stool, or if you cannot pass stool or gas.
warning_signs_to_escalate: severe abdominal pain; vomiting; blood in stool; swollen belly
